To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spectroscopic factors for the removal of the last neutron from the N=16 isotopes are significantly reduced from the values expected from a simple shell model.

(1) one-neutron knockout on the N=16 isotonic chain is an effective tool for the spectroscopic study of the N=16 sub-shell closure, (2) the one-neutron reduced single-particle occupancy is significantly reduced with respect to the shell-model predictions for the deeply bound nuclei in the chain, (3) the spectroscopic factors for the ground states of the N=15 isotonic chain follow the same trend as the ones observed for the ground states for the N=16

the spectroscopic factors of the N=16 isotone series show a strong decrease from O-20 to Ne-20, and that the reduced single-particle occupancy of the N=20 neutron is found to be similar to that of the N=14 and N=18 neutron.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the evolution of the structure of proton-rich nuclei in the region of the N=20 shell closure, which has attracted much interest in the last years.
the spectroscopic properties of the proton-rich N=16 isotone chain.
the spectroscopy of exotic nuclei and the study of nuclear structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reduced spectroscopic factors observed in one-nucleont knockout reactions from N=16 isotonic nuclei are a result of both the short-range correlations and the coupling to the final-state continuum.
, while the systematics of the spectroscopic factors is consistent with the short-range correlations, the angular momentum distributions do not show the expected trend.

the spectroscopic factors extracted in this work for the one-neutron knockout reaction from the N=16 isotone region are systematically smaller than the USD shell-model predictions, which are known to reproduce well other experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the systematics of spectroscopic factors and single-particle occupances are consistent with the shell-model predictions.
the spectroscopic factors and the momentum distributions are in good agreement with shell-model calculations.
the spectroscopic factors are reduced by a factor of 2 to 3 with respect to the shell-model predictions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reduced spectroscopic factor is a function of both the binding energy of the removed particle and the binding energy of its parent nucleus.
, in spite of the large neutron separation energies, one-neutron knockout reactions are a powerful tool to probe the single-particle structure of proton-rich nuclei.

the systematics of reduced spectroscopic factors observed in (p,2p) and (He-3,2p) reactions on light nuclei with N=16 is not observed in one-nucleus knockout on the proton-rich isotones with Z = 16, 17, and 16.
